title: bounds
summary: Return smallest and largest elements in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Delegates to the existing `min` and `max` reduction engines, including their GPU fallbacks and host execution paths.

description: `bounds(A)` returns the smallest and largest values from each slice of `A` along the first non-singleton dimension.
behaviors: `[S,L] = bounds(A)` returns the same values as `min(A)` and `max(A)` using the default dimension.
`bounds(A,'all')` reduces all elements and returns scalar lower and upper bounds.
`bounds` omits NaN values by default, matching MATLAB. Pass `'includenan'` to propagate NaN values consistently with `min` and `max`.
Logical, integer, real, complex, scalar, vector, matrix, N-D, and GPU tensor inputs follow the behavior of the underlying `min` and `max` builtins.

examples.description: Bounds across all elements while ignoring NaN by default

faqs.question: How many outputs does `bounds` return?
faqs.answer: It returns two outputs: the smallest values and the largest values. RunMat pads additional requested outputs with zero, matching the runtime's multi-output convention.

faqs.question: Does `bounds` have separate GPU kernels?
faqs.answer: No. It composes `min` and `max`, so it inherits their GPU support and host fallback behavior.
